one_liner: Datadog has a broad REST API authenticated with an API key plus application key headers; OAuth is limited to approved partners, so third parties use keys. Access needs a Datadog org account, and the pages don't settle trial versus free.
auth_notes: The API docs say to authenticate with an API key in the DD-API-KEY header, and some endpoints also need an application key in DD-APPLICATION-KEY. OAuth 2.0 exists but only for approved Technology Partners; standalone OAuth clients are not supported, so OAUTH2 is removed from the third-party methods. Personal access tokens were mentioned in the draft, but no supplied page confirms them. Datadog orgs live on regional sites/domains, so the site must be configured per customer.
access_notes: No supplied page says how a developer gets keys or whether a free tier exists. Keys come from an org account, so a trial or paid account is assumed. The partner sandbox is for Technology Partners only. Low confidence on trial versus free.
blocker_notes: Third parties cannot use OAuth, so each customer must create and supply API and application keys and the correct regional site. An account that can create keys (trial or paid) is also needed. The pages do not verify the MCP server. The official rating rests on the draft and on Composio listing a Datadog MCP toolkit.

evidence.quote: The Datadog API is an HTTP REST API.
OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners developing official Datadog integrations. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.
Access to a Datadog sandbox for development and testing
Integrations that only query Datadog data can be supported through our public APIs
